candidates.evidence: Two modes at 360.30 and 420.31 cm-1 (FWHM 3.4 and 5.8 cm-1). Literature WS2 E^1_2g is about 356-357 cm-1 and A1g about 420-421 cm-1 (bulk), with monolayer near 355-356 and 418-419 (Berkdemir et al. 2013, values recalled, not re-checked). A1g matches well. E' is about 3-5 cm-1 high and the splitting is 60.0 cm-1 versus about 62-64 cm-1 typical, so the match is good but not exact.

MoS2 literature E^1_2g is about 383 cm-1 and A1g about 408 cm-1 (Lee et al., ACS Nano 2010, recalled). Observed modes are off by more than 20 cm-1 each, and the splitting would be about 25 cm-1 versus 60 observed.
WSe2 Raman-active modes lie near 250 cm-1 (recalled). No intense feature there; the strongest peaks are at 360 and 420 cm-1.
MoSe2 first-order modes lie near 240 and 287 cm-1 (recalled). Neither is present; the strongest peaks are at 360 and 420 cm-1.

peaks.source: Lorentzian fit 320-460 cm-1, centre 360.296 +/- 0.014 cm-1 (statistical only). Assignment from literature: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), WS2 E^1_2g near 356-357 cm-1 (recalled, not re-checked).

Lorentzian fit 320-460 cm-1, centre 420.312 +/- 0.10 cm-1. Assignment from literature: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013), WS2 A1g near 420 cm-1 bulk and 418-419 cm-1 monolayer (recalled, not re-checked).

properties.name: phase
properties.source: The E^1_2g + A1g pair at 360/420 cm-1 is the 2H-WS2 signature; 2H is the common WS2 polytype (Berkdemir et al. 2013, recalled).

properties.name: layers
properties.source: A1g at 420.3 cm-1 is closer to bulk (420-421) than monolayer (418-419) literature values; the splitting of 60.0 cm-1 is slightly below typical values, so the thickness call is not reliable from this spectrum alone.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: E^1_2g FWHM is 3.4 cm-1, which suggests good crystallinity. This is a rough inference from one linewidth; no defect-activated modes were looked for.

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.source: The E' mode sits about 3-5 cm-1 above typical WS2 values, which could indicate compressive strain or calibration error, but the data cannot separate these.

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: No doping-sensitive feature was analysed (e.g. A1g/E' intensity or width changes); the data do not constrain it.

citations: Berkdemir, A. et al. Identification of individual and few layers of WS2 using Raman spectroscopy. Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013). (WS2 E^1_2g and A1g positions and layer dependence; values recalled from memory, not re-checked in this session)

Lee, C. et al. Anomalous lattice vibrations of single- and few-layer MoS2. ACS Nano 4, 2695 (2010). (MoS2 E^1_2g about 383 and A1g about 408 cm-1 used as the alternative-material comparison; recalled, not re-checked)
limits: Verdict is consistency, not identification. No reference spectrum was available and the literature numbers were recalled from memory, not checked against the papers.

Wavenumber calibration cannot be verified: the window 60-1100 cm-1 contains no Si line at 520.7 cm-1 and substrate is null. The E' mode sits about 3-5 cm-1 above typical WS2 values while A1g matches; a uniform calibration offset would move both, so a simple offset does not explain it. Strain, doping, thickness or my recalled reference values could account for it, and the data cannot distinguish these.
Splitting E'-A1g = 60.0 cm-1 is slightly below the usual 62-64 cm-1 for WS2. This is a mismatch I cannot resolve without a reference spectrum.
Polarization and collection geometry are not given, so the E'/A1g intensity ratio (height ratio about 0.18, area ratio about 0.30) cannot be interpreted. No angle-resolved analysis was possible.
Layer number cannot be determined reliably from peak positions alone.
Second-order and low-frequency bands (2LA(M) near 351 cm-1, LA(M) near 178 cm-1) were not detected above noise. Their absence does not contradict WS2 but gives no positive support.

Weak features at about 193.5, 231.6 and 844.9 cm-1 reach only about 4-5 sigma in the smoothed residual (noise sigma about 165 counts, residual white, lag-1 autocorrelation -0.01). They are not reported as peaks and are unassigned.

The broad background rising from about 2000 counts at 60 cm-1 to about 9000 near 800 cm-1 and falling to about 7600 at 1100 cm-1 has no identified origin (fluorescence or substrate background are possibilities). It was removed by asymmetric least-squares baseline before fitting.
A single-pixel spike at 162.56 cm-1 (20744 counts against about 2800 neighbours) was replaced by its neighbour median before baseline and peak fitting. No other spikes were found.
Data span is 60-1100 cm-1 only; WS2 signatures above 1100 cm-1 were not checked.
